summary: xAI's Grok Build coding agent, driven in a terminal.

manual.$comment: Grok has the same permission modes Claude Code does (`grok --help`: `--permission-mode [default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan]`). No --trust: that would trust the hooks committed in the repository, which run commands nobody is asked about.
manual.label: Default
manual.description: Grok’s default mode: it asks before every edit and every command.

acceptEdits.$comment: Grok's own Accept edits mode, at the Auto level, as for Claude Code. No --trust, for the reason given on manual.
acceptEdits.label: Accept edits
acceptEdits.description: Grok’s Accept edits mode: file edits in the workspace go through without asking, and commands ask first.

auto.$comment: Grok's own `auto` mode, as Claude Code's Auto is (owner ruling 2026-10-01): a person who picks Auto expects the CLI's auto mode, and acceptEdits asked before every command. No --trust, for the reason given on manual; like a launch with no flag, a Grok agent that does not trust the project's hooks sends no agent-state frames, until trust is granted in the TUI with /hooks-trust.
auto.label: Auto
auto.summary: Grok runs what it judges safe; blocks the rest.
auto.description: Grok’s own auto mode: a classifier runs the tool calls it judges safe and turns the risky ones back to Grok.

dontAsk.$comment: Grok's own Don't ask mode, at the Manual level, as for Claude Code. No --trust, for the reason given on manual.
dontAsk.label: Don’t ask
dontAsk.summary: Never asks; refuses what your rules don’t allow.
dontAsk.description: Grok’s Don’t ask mode: it never stops to ask, and turns down every tool call your own allow rules do not already cover.

bypass.$comment: --trust rides this preset, never the default launch argv: it does not just enable the studio's own .grok/hooks agent-state reporter — it trusts EVERY project-level .grok config, including hooks committed in the repo itself, so a freshly cloned untrusted repo must not get it when the person chose to pass no permission flag. Without trust Grok skips project hooks, so no frames arrive and the session converts to the stalled phase via the runtime watchdog (there is no output-timing fallback any more); the user can grant trust in the TUI via /hooks-trust. Kept as `--always-approve` rather than switched to `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`: both exist in `grok --help`, and this one is what shipped and is covered by tests.
bypass.label: Always approve
bypass.summary: Approves every tool call. Trusted repos only.
bypass.description: Grok’s --always-approve: every tool call runs without asking, and the project’s own Grok configuration is trusted. Use only in repositories you trust.

promptInjection.$comment: Verified 2026-09-24 against the installed Grok Build 1.0.41: `grok --help` prints `Usage: grok [OPTIONS] [PROMPT] [COMMAND]` and documents [PROMPT] as "Initial prompt for the interactive session, e.g. `grok "fix the bug"`", so the first message rides the command line like Claude Code's. It goes after `--` because the same position also takes a subcommand: `grok version` printed the version and exited, while `grok -- version` opened the TUI with `version` as its prompt, so without the separator a one-word first message such as `update` or `logout` would run that command instead, and one starting with `-` would be read as an option. Not verified end to end with a signed-in session (that would spend tokens).

overflow.$comment: A first message too long for the platform's command line is typed in: launched without it, then pasted (bracketed) and submitted once the TUI is reading. `--no-auto-update` rides only that launch. Grok 1.0.41's startup update check can stop at `Update now? [Y/n/d]`, where the typed Enter would accept the default and install the update; the binary's bundled docs list `--no-auto-update` (session scope) under Update Check Suppression, and 1.0.41 accepts it (`grok --no-auto-update --version` printed the version, where an unknown option is refused).

contextInjection.$comment: grok --append-system-prompt <text>, verified accepted by the installed Grok Build 1.0.13 as an undocumented compat alias of the documented --rules ("Extra rules to append to the system prompt"). Text rather than a file: grok documents no file-taking variant. Spread into launch AND resume argv, so a resumed session is re-told. Re-verified 2026-09-24 against Grok Build 1.0.25: --help documents --rules and --system-prompt-override (both text) and --prompt-file only for a single-turn run; the binary's strings hold no rules-file or append-system-prompt-file flag. A document too long for the platform's command line is cut instead, with a marker naming the file main wrote it to (planAgentLaunch in src/main/agent-launch-render.ts).

installTargets.$comment: restartRequired NOT verified on 2026-07-29: the probe could not reach an interactive session because this machine is not signed in to Grok (the TUI sits on its browser-approval screen). Left true — a banner that over-warns is recoverable, one that under-warns is not. Verify by adding a skill directory while `grok` runs and checking its /skill picker.

agentStateSpec.$comment: Grok Build ships Claude-style lifecycle hooks. Discovery is per-file: project hooks are standalone JSON files under .grok/hooks/, so we own our config file outright (owned-json). Project hooks only run once the folder is trusted — see the bypass_all $comment. VERIFIED 2026-09-09 against grok 1.0.13 (xAI's Grok Build TUI at /opt/homebrew/bin/grok — NOT the community `grok-cli`, whose hook engine fires only for its bash tool), by reading the hook reference embedded in the binary and by writing candidate .grok/hooks/*.json files and counting what `grok inspect` loaded. CONFIG spelling: the event names below are written PascalCase and grok loads them (15/15 in a probe file). It also accepts snake_case and Cursor camelCase, but NOT kebab-case or SCREAMING, and it silently skips names it does not know — so this is a fixed alias set, not case-insensitivity, and our PascalCase is inside it. PAYLOAD spelling differs from the config spelling: the documented stdin payload stamps "hookEventName": "pre_tool_use" (snake_case), while field NAMES are camelCase (hookEventName / sessionId / toolName / toolInput, each with a snake_case serde alias the shared reporter also reads). That mismatch was a real bug: the main process compared this manifest's PascalCase to the frame's snake_case EXACTLY and dropped every Grok frame, so a Grok agent never left `starting` until the stall watch flagged it. Fixed in resolveAgentStateEvent by canonical (case- and _/- insensitive) comparison, so the table below keeps grok's own written form and the registration emitter still writes it verbatim. Grok's documented Notification types are `idle_prompt`, `permission_prompt`, `task_complete`: `permission_prompt` below is CONFIRMED real, `elicitation_dialog` and `agent_needs_input` are harmless carry-over grok never sends, and `idle_prompt` stays off the list deliberately (a false needs-input parks a session forever; a false idle is recoverable). NOT verified live: no payload was captured from a running session — this machine is not signed in to Grok (`grok -p` exits "Not signed in"), so whether a file edit fires PreToolUse/PostToolUse, and the edit tool's name in a real payload, still rest on the embedded docs (which name grok's edit tool `search_replace`, aliased from Edit/Write/MultiEdit; Bash is `run_terminal_command`). Grok also ships events this table does not use yet: PostToolUseFailure, PermissionDenied, StopFailure, StopCancelled, SubagentStart, PreCompact, PostCompact.

selfUpdate.$comment: Verified 2026-10-13 against Grok Build 1.0.41: `grok --help` lists `update` ("Check for updates or install a specific version") and `grok update --help` documents `--check`, `--version` and the channel switches, so a bare `grok update` installs the latest stable build. It downloads into ~/.grok/bin and moves the `grok` link there, which is where the official installer puts it; an npm install of the same CLI is updated with npm instead (chooseCliUpdateCommand), since this would leave the npm copy first on PATH.

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (the confirm-first discipline: an unverified resume path must not risk a lost conversation). Grok Build documents claude-style resume (-s/--session-id at launch, -r/--resume <id> on relaunch) and the resume argv above is wired for it, so once resume is verified against a real Grok Build install, flip this to true — no code change needed. sessionIdFromCaller is true because launch passes our minted --session-id.
